LHX.sentence: L3Harris has fallen about 28% from its high, which is unusually steep for a steady defense company, especially while the rest of the defense sector is doing well — so nothing about the business has really changed, it's just out of favor.

ASML.sentence: ASML has pulled back a bit, but it's still the only company on earth that makes the machines needed to print the most advanced chips, so nothing about its position has shifted.

LIN.sentence: Linde is having a flat, uneventful week — they supply oxygen, nitrogen and other industrial gases on long contracts and nudge prices up a little each quarter, which is the whole quiet story with this one.

MSFT.sentence: Microsoft is calm — the stock is fully priced and barely off its highs, and the AI-cloud story keeps grinding along without any drama.

TMO.sentence: Thermo Fisher dipped again; it sells the equipment and supplies that labs and drugmakers run on, and that demand is scraping along a low point right now — the kind of lull that usually comes before a recovery.

CVX.sentence: Chevron rose with oil prices, which are swollen because fighting involving Iran has disrupted Persian Gulf shipments — so these are unusually fat profits from the oil price, not from anything the company itself did better.

NOW.sentence: ServiceNow is down sharply from its high, more than 40%, even as big companies and government agencies keep signing up for its workflow and AI-assistant tools on long contracts — so the business looks fine and the stock has just gotten cheaper.

GLNCY.sentence: Glencore edged up and is holding up better than copper prices themselves — its giant commodity-trading arm tends to make money when markets are choppy, which cushions the blow when metal prices sag.

MLM.sentence: Martin Marietta slipped a touch, but the price it gets per ton of crushed rock is still creeping up year over year — its quarries each quietly own their patch of the map, which is the part that actually matters.

KOF.sentence: Coca-Cola FEMSA drifted down mostly because the Mexican peso weakened, which shrinks the value of its earnings when converted to dollars — the bottling business itself is steady, this is just a currency headwind.

UBER.sentence: Uber dipped, but people are booking more rides than ever, and there's still no sign that self-driving cars are pulling business away — so for now it's a worry about the future, not a problem today.

AMKBY.sentence: Maersk ticked up and is trading below what it would cost to replace its own fleet of ships — a rock-bottom valuation that often marks the floor for this kind of shipping company, which moves containers around the world and reflects the health of global trade.

MA.sentence: Mastercard slipped slightly, but people keep tapping their cards more than ever and the business is growing a touch faster than Visa's — this is a steady toll-taker with nothing broken.

ISRG.sentence: The surgical robot company is down meaningfully from its high even though hospitals keep doing more procedures with its machines — and since most of its money comes from the supplies each operation uses, the underlying business is still humming.

NVDA.sentence: Nvidia dropped almost 6% after Google's parent and Amazon showed they're now spending more on computing gear than their businesses bring in and borrowing the rest — nothing changed at Nvidia itself, but those companies are its biggest customers, so whether they can keep paying is the whole question.
